overview: Tenacity 6.0's ScaffoldModule splits its work across three events. The MotionEvent pre phase resolves the block cache below the player, gcd-quantizes the module's target yaw/pitch into the movement packet, applies a 0.91 horizontal motion decay on ground ('or else watchdog will delete your blocks') and runs the tower motion; BlockPlaceableEvent, dispatched once per tick from the fork's Minecraft.runTick, fires the placement through the vanilla player controller using the previous tick's cache; and the packet listener suppresses vanilla C09s in Server switch mode while the module's own C09s go out through a no-event path. The four tower modes collapse to two: the Verus and Vulcan branches are nested inside the BlocksMC case, so selecting them executes nothing. Rotations are silent: the pre-phase write carries them into the C03 while the post event mirrors them into the head model.

sections.p: The MotionEvent handler runs in the pre phase. It resolves the block slot with InventoryUtil.getBlockSlot, forces the sprint key when the sprint setting is on (the vanilla sprint path then emits C0B as sprint state changes) and clears it otherwise, and switches items: Client mode writes mc.thePlayer.inventory.currentItem directly with no packet, Server mode queues C09PacketHeldItemChange through addToSendQueueNoEvent and records lastSlot, while the packet listener cancels every vanilla C09 that crosses the event bus in Server mode and stashes its slot as startSlot. getBlockCache probes the cell at posY - 1 and, when it is air, scans a square of radius searchRange with alternating +-i sweeps, checking the six neighbors of each air cell for a solid non-liquid material and returning the first BlockCache with the opposite face. The target yaw/pitch are gcd-quantized (fixedYaw = yaw - yaw % sensitivityMultiplier, same for pitch) and written into the pre event, which the fork's EntityPlayerSP folds into the C03 variant send; the post event then mirrors them into rotationYawHead and rotationPitchHead. On ground the module multiplies motionX and motionZ by 0.91 every tick, a deliberate slowdown the comment attributes to Watchdog block deletion.

placeBlock runs from BlockPlaceableEvent, which Minecraft.runTick dispatches once per tick after the movement and right-click handling. It uses lastBlockCache, the cache from the previous tick, so the placement lags the block search by one tick; onPlayerRightClick is called with that position, face and the getHitVec vector (block center plus 0.5, an extra 0.5 on horizontal faces, 0.3 on vertical faces, plus 0.15 axis tweaks), which emits C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement and runs the local onItemUse. On success the module calls updateRotations, which recomputes the aim for the next tick's C03, and swings: Client mode calls swingItem, and the fork's EntityPlayerSP.swingItem queues C0APacketAnimation, while Server mode queues the C0A directly. Rotation modes: Enum snaps yaw to angleFromEnumFacing() - 180 (the cardinal index times 90, minus 180) at pitch 77; Brute Force RayCast scans yaw and pitch in bruteForceRayCastIntensity steps until a ray from that look hits the target cell. onDisable restores the start slot through the same switch path.

The tower switch runs inside the pre phase when the jump key is held and a block cache exists. Vanilla sets motionY to 0.42 on every such tick. BlocksMC sets 0.42 while space is held and 0.15 while any movement key is held. The Verus and Vulcan branches are nested inside the BlocksMC case, so their code only executes when towerMode is exactly BlocksMC: a user selecting Verus or Vulcan gets no tower at all. The Verus branch itself would randomize motionY between 0.4 and 0.5 and toggle C0BPacketEntityAction sprint state every tick with a serverSprintState bookkeeping bug that writes false in both branches, and both branches warn through ChatUtil after 4 seconds of use. The net effect is that only two tower profiles exist in practice: the per-tick 0.42 re-apply and the 0.15 moving climb.

files.label: ScaffoldModule.java
files.explanation: The complete module: the three event listeners (MotionEvent pre-phase cache and rotation, BlockPlaceableEvent placement, PacketSendEvent C09 suppression), the switch item modes, the BlockCache inner class and its ring search, the Enum and Brute Force RayCast rotation modes, getHitVec, the sprint forcing, the 0.91 ground motion decay, and the tower switch with its nested-case bug that makes the Verus and Vulcan modes unreachable.

files.label: EntityPlayerSP.java (motion event and swing hooks)
files.explanation: The fork hook the module's two silent mechanisms ride on. The motion dispatch (line 242) fires the pre MotionEvent, then sends the C03 variant (C06 PosLook, C04 Position, C05 Look or plain C03) using the event's x/y/z, yaw, pitch and ground flag, then fires the post event, and finally mirrors the event rotations into rotationYawHead and rotationPitchHead, so the module's pre-phase writes reach the server while the local rotationYaw stays untouched. The swingItem override at line 337 calls super.swingItem and queues C0APacketAnimation, which is why the Client swing mode still emits a C0A.

countering.label: NCP blockplace Scaffold check (angle / time / sprint / tool-switch)
countering.explanation: The bridging-profile gate (horizontal face, block 1-2 below, solid, within 2.0 blocks) applies, and the sub-checks hit Tenacity's fixed profiles hard. Angle compares the look against the placed face normal and flags above MAX_ANGLE 90 degrees: the Enum rotation mode holds pitch 77 against an UP face normal, a look-versus-normal angle of 103 degrees, so every placement flags, and the Brute Force mode only escapes when its scan happens to find a look within the threshold. Time records placement ticks at pitch over 70 with no sneak and no speed potion and flags the average interval below scaffoldTimeAvg: the module places once per tick at pitch 77, so the average sits near 1 tick and the violation fires, and there is no sneak emulation to refresh NCP's sneakTime exemption. Sprint flags placements within 8 ticks of sprinting at yDistance under 0.1 and jumpPhase under 4, and the sprint setting is on by default, forcing the C0B sprint state while placing. ToolSwitch flags held-slot changes between placements, and the Server switch mode's explicit C09s produce exactly that on any mixed hotbar.

countering.label: NCP blockplace FastPlace (placement rate window)
countering.explanation: FastPlace accumulates accepted placements into an ActionFrequency(2, 1000) two-second window plus a short-term tick counter and flags when the window score exceeds cc.fastPlaceLimit. BlockPlaceableEvent fires once per tick and placeBlock emits one C08 when the cache and slot resolve, about 20 per second, which holds the window several times over the limit for the whole bridge. The module has no place-delay dial to spread placements, and the 0.91 ground motion decay does not change the packet rate, only the horizontal speed, so the rate is exactly one C08 per tick. The short-term counter is what catches a lag spike that batches two client ticks into one server tick.

countering.label: NCP blockplace Direction (look ray vs clicked face)
countering.explanation: Direction ray-traces from the eye with the server-side yaw/pitch of the last C03 against the claimed clicked block and accumulates the angular deviation into directionVL with a 0.9 per-tick decay. Tenacity's aim is structurally one tick stale: the C03 look of tick N is computed by updateRotations after the placement of tick N-1, targeting the block from that tick, so on a straight bridge the stale look still crosses the face below and the check stays quiet, but on turns and direction changes the server ray lags a full tick behind the face being clicked, and directionVL accumulates on every such placement. The Brute Force mode only refreshes the aim when its step scan finds the target cell; when it does not, the previous yaw/pitch persist into the next placement. Because the module places every tick, violations outrun the 0.9 decay whenever the aim is stale.

countering.label: NCP SurvivalFly (jump envelope vs tower)
countering.explanation: SurvivalFly's jump envelope credits one impulse per MAX_JUMP_DELAY = 10 ticks, requiring the yDistance to match the predicted jump gain with a from-ground state read from the block cache. The Vanilla tower re-asserts motionY 0.42 on every pre tick while the jump key is held and a cache exists, not only on ground ticks, so the first impulse is credited and every following re-assertion inside the window falls to the momentum prediction, yielding a yDistanceAboveLimit around 0.32 and a violation of 30+ with a set-back. The BlocksMC 0.15 climb is a sub-jump vertical that the envelope never credits, so it flags on the same axis. The Verus and Vulcan profiles never run because of the nested-case bug, so their 0.4-0.5 and 0.2 motionY variants are moot. The 0.91 ground decay is the compensating trade: it keeps horizontal motion under the predicted sprint envelope, so the horizontal side stays quiet while the vertical re-apply is the tell.
